ai.description: The Mugger grows to 4–5m. It is olive-grey to brown with a broad, rounded snout. It features 19 rows of dorsal scales and four large post-occipital scutes arranged in a square.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Mugger crocodile is best distinguished by its broad, robust snout, which is significantly wider than the slender, elongated snouts of the sympatric Saltwater or Gharial.
ai.habitat: The Mugger inhabits freshwater environments like marshes, lakes, and slow-moving rivers, typically below 500m elevation, often surrounded by dense riparian vegetation.
ai.behavior: The mugger crocodile is primarily a nocturnal hunter that uses its powerful tail to ambush prey, often employing "lure" behavior by balancing sticks on its snout.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Crocodylus palustris* is oviparous, nesting annually during the dry season (Dec–April). Females lay 20–40 eggs in excavated riverbank pits, which hatch after 55–75 days.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Mugger crocodile inhabits freshwater habitats across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from sea level to 600m in diverse biogeographic zones like the Indo-Gangetic plain.
